entities.summary: Charles Borromeo was an Italian Catholic prelate who served as Archbishop of Milan from 1564 to 1584. He was made a cardinal in 1560. Borromeo played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation, a Catholic movement aimed at revitalizing the faith in Europe during the 16th century. He introduced various reforms, including the creation of a new catechism, the establishment of orphanages and hospitals, and the promotion of education. Borromeo's efforts helped to increase the number of Catholic clergy and reform the Catholic Church's liturgical practices. The reforms he implemented had a lasting impact on the Catholic Church and its relationship with the Italian state. Borromeo's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing subsequent Catholic leaders and shaping the Church's approach to social welfare and education. He is remembered for his dedication to his faith and his efforts to strengthen the Catholic Church in Italy. Borromeo's impact on the Catholic Church and Italian society is still felt today, with many of the reforms he implemented continuing to influence Catholic practice and policy.
